name: UptimeRobot
summary: UptimeRobot's free plan covers 50 monitors checked every 5 minutes, and its terms allow commercial use. Paid plans start at $10 a month ($9 on annual billing), add checks every minute or faster, and offer checks from up to four regions. SMS and voice credits are sold separately.

evidence.capability: http and ping checks from multiple locations

facts.text: UptimeRobot's terms say the service is available for any use, including commercial and business use.
Paid monitors can run from up to four regions: North America, Europe, Asia and Australia. A monitor with no region chosen is checked from North America.
Paid upgrades renew automatically, and can be cancelled at any time in the My Settings section of the dashboard.
The Enterprise page lists SSO/SAML as included on the Enterprise plan, and says UptimeRobot has completed an independent SOC 2 audit and lists SOC 2 Type I.

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: 50 monitors at 5-minute intervals, 1 status page, no login seats

plans.name: Solo
plans.notes: Shown as $9 a month on annual billing. 60-second checks. The monitor count shown on the page is not consistent

plans.name: Team
plans.notes: Shown as $35 a month on annual billing. 100 monitors at 30-second checks, 3 login seats

plans.name: Scale
plans.notes: Shown as $65 a month on annual billing. 200 monitors at 15-second checks, 5 login seats

hiddenCosts: SMS and voice credits are one-time packs: $3 for 10 credits, $15 for 100, $25 for 200, $55 for 500 and $100 for 1,000.

contract.cancellation: Upgrades can be cancelled at any time in My Settings. Auto-renewal runs until the subscription is cancelled.
